_comment: Single source of truth for the iris geometry pipeline. Both implementations (iris-geometry.js for the browser, app.py for the Flask/OpenCV path) MUST agree with these values. tests/test_geometry.py asserts that they do, so the two twins cannot drift silently the way they did before (webapp.html had lost eyelid masking entirely).

unwrap._comment: Raw polar->rectangular output, 25 px per ring across 12 rings. The grid renderer resamples this into the non-uniform ring bands below.

pupil._comment: Adaptive threshold replaces the old hard-coded value of 40, which merged pupil and iris on dark brown eyes and silently corrupted every downstream coordinate. Several dark-fractions are tried as competing hypotheses and the first whose pupil+iris pair passes the validity gate wins, because on a dark iris a single fraction can swallow the whole iris disc into the 'pupil'.

eyelid._comment: Lid candidate points are searched across the whole iris annulus above/below the pupil, not just a thin band near the rim. With the old narrow band a half-closed eye produced no lid fit at all, so it was silently treated as fully visible and lid skin was analysed as iris.

roll._comment: Camera/head roll is recovered from the two canthi (eye corners), found as the intersections of the fitted upper and lower eyelid curves. Without this, minute 0 is 'up in the image' rather than anatomical up, so a typical phone-selfie tilt shifted every sector by up to half a zone.
